description: The bar chart presents the Shapley values for three different models—mBERT, XLM-R, and chLSTM—across various categories labeled from L_4^+ to R_4^+. The horizontal axis lists the categories, while the vertical axis measures the Shapley value on a linear scale from 0 to 80, with tick intervals of 20 units. Each category has a group of three bars, each representing one of the models, with mBERT in light blue, XLM-R in dark blue, and chLSTM in green. The highest values are observed in category T, with mBERT at approximately 50, XLM-R at about 70, and chLSTM at the maximum value of 80. In contrast, the other categories such as L_4^+, L_3, L_2, L_1, R_1, R_2, R_3, and R_4^+ show much shorter bars, generally below 15. The bars for R_1 are notably taller than those for L_1, suggesting a stronger contribution from the right context in R_1. The chart includes a legend in the top right corner to identify the models corresponding to each color.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the Shapley value for different models across various categories. The horizontal axis represents the categories labeled as L_4^+, L_3, L_2, L_1, T, R_1, R_2, R_3, R_4^+, while the vertical axis represents the 'Shapley value,' measured on a linear scale from 0 to 80 with tick intervals of 20 units. Bars are grouped by category, with each group containing three bars representing different models: mBERT (light blue), XLM-R (dark blue), and chLSTM (green). The tallest bars appear in category T, where mBERT has an approximate value of 50, XLM-R about 70, and chLSTM reaching the maximum value of 80. In other categories such as L_4^+, L_3, L_2, L_1, R_1, R_2, R_3, and R_4^+, the bars are all relatively short, generally below 15. Notably, the values for R_1 consistently exceed those for L_1 across all models, indicating a stronger contribution from the right context. A legend is provided in the top right corner.
